scenarios.title: Drifts sideways between 25,000 and 25,200
watch: Two daily closes below 25,200 without a new high
Close - open (the body) small, either colour
scenarios.means: The move is pausing. Time decay is working for the seller.
scenarios.action: Hold. Add a bear call spread: sell 25,300 CE, buy 25,500 CE (credit about 65 pts, Rs 4,250 per lot; max loss Rs 8,750) to turn it into an iron condor.

scenarios.title: Reaches 25,200 and stalls
watch: High - close bigger than close - low (sellers took it back)
25,200 CE open interest still rising (call writers defending)
scenarios.means: Call writers are defending 25,200. A ceiling for now.
scenarios.action: Sell a bear call spread at 25,300 (sell 25,300 CE / buy 25,500 CE). Roll the put spread up to sell 25,100 PE / buy 24,800 PE to lock in what the rise earned.

scenarios.title: Breaks out above 25,200
watch: 25,200 CE open interest falling (writers buying back - short covering)
Close near the day's high again
scenarios.means: The ceiling gave way. Next magnets: 25,300 then 25,500.
scenarios.action: Do not sell calls at 25,300. Roll the put spread up to sell 25,200 PE / buy 24,900 PE. Sell calls only at 25,500 or above. If it spikes past 25,300 in one session with VIX rising, take profit instead of chasing.
scenarios.odds: Reached 25,300 in 64.4% and 25,500 in 42.5% of past cases (normal 63.3% / 42.5%).

scenarios.title: Pulls back to 25,000
watch: Holds: daily close above 25,000 and 25,000 PE open interest still rising
Breaks: daily close below 25,000 and 25,000 PE open interest falling
scenarios.means: A test of the put writers' floor. Shakeouts are normal after strong runs.
scenarios.action: If it holds: keep the position. If it breaks: exit the put spread (loss capped and known) and flip to a bear call spread, sell 25,100 CE / buy 25,300 CE. Next floors 24,500 then 24,100.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 25,000 at some point in 56.2% of past cases (normal 59.1%).

rules: Take profit on any spread once 50% of its credit is earned; the rest is not worth the risk.
Close any spread once its loss reaches 1.5x the credit taken, whatever day that is. Holding into expiry is fine; size smaller on expiry day.
Act on daily closes, not intraday spikes. The OI checks use the next morning's bhavcopy.
Credits for rolls and add-ons are set by prices on the day you act; today's numbers are a guide only.
limits: None of the desk's positioning signals (PCR, max pain, OI flow, walls) has passed its own backtest for this horizon, so the history study is the main evidence.
